endorsements.quote: That might mean integrating retrieval-augmented models linked to vetted guideline repositories, offering AI-assisted frequently asked questions (FAQs) within patient portals, or explicitly encouraging patients to bring AI-generated questions to visits so that they can be discussed in context.

unlisted_practices: Channel patient curiosity toward safer, health-system-vetted AI resources rather than relying solely on defensive messaging such as 'do not trust what you read online'.
Encourage patients to bring AI-generated questions to clinical visits so they can be discussed in context.
Conduct prospective empirical research on whether AI-mediated patient education improves shared decision-making, safety, and equity and whether it influences clinician behaviour.
Do not treat AI as a replacement for clinician counselling or as a stand-alone arbiter of truth.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual commentary/perspective article introducing the concept of the 'AI-educated patient' and discussing potential mechanisms, risks, and implications without presenting empirical data.
